act_on.irregularity: Measurement rows are valves, and some animals contribute two valves.
act_on.evidence: catalogue.csv contains 72 specimen IDs belonging to 52 individual IDs: 20 animals have both L and R valves. For example, I052 appears at lines 4 and 10 as V41347 and V51064; their measurements occur at measurements.csv lines 28 and 32.
act_on.inference: A regression using all 72 rows would weight paired animals twice and report the wrong number of individuals.
act_on.handling: Join measurements to the catalogue by specimen_id and construct one length–height observation per individual. A defensible default is to average available valve lengths and heights within each animal, then log10-transform and fit the reduced-major-axis regression using 52 individuals.

leave_alone: Paired valves have slightly different measurements; retain that information when forming individual summaries rather than treating the records as erroneous duplicates.
Catalogue and measurement ordering differs, but specimen IDs join completely and uniquely.
Two localities are represented; the task requests a pooled regression and supplies no requirement for separate locality fits.
items.notes: The materials do not specify how paired valves should represent an individual. Arithmetic averaging before logging, averaging logged values, or selecting one valve can yield different coefficients; the chosen rule must be stated. The referenced answer.schema.json is absent.
